monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — evidenced by faster paces, higher HR, more Z3–Z4 time, and improved aerobic efficiency and cadence.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.8 — the largest single-month gain in your log — reflecting improved running economy at similar or faster paces despite lower weekly volume.

goal_tracker.message: You need 8.3 more km across 3 remaining sessions — e.g., one 4km, one 3km, and one 1.3km run — to match last month’s distance. Prioritize consistency over intensity in these sessions to avoid fatigue accumulation.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved +0.38 (13.42 → 13.8) even as avg pace quickened by 36 sec/km and avg HR rose +7 bpm — indicating better oxygen utilization and neuromuscular coordination at faster efforts.

insights.title: Shift toward threshold and tempo work
insights.body: Zone 3 time increased from 19% to 27%, Zone 4 from 3% to 16%, and Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 54% — signaling a deliberate move away from pure base-building toward lactate threshold development.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff observed
insights.body: Cadence rose +6 spm (146 → 152), yet stride length decreased (e.g., 94.7 → 69.5 cm on long runs), suggesting you’re favoring quicker turnover over reach — beneficial for fatigue resistance but may limit top-end speed development without strength support.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Three of your five recent runs (6/7, 6/11, 6/16) delivered Aerobic TE ≥3.4, yet only one was preceded by >48h rest — and your longest run (11.1km) came just 5 days after another 11.0km run — increasing cumulative strain risk.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a 5km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~9:10–9:30/km) with cadence consciously held at 150–152 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 time dropped sharply (43% → 34%) and avg HR rose — this session restores aerobic stimulus while reinforcing efficient turnover without accumulating fatigue.

recommendations.action: Perform a 10-minute post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexors and calves after every run this week, especially following sessions with ground contact time >310ms (e.g., your 6/7 and 6/16 long runs).
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time averaged 314ms and 317ms on your two longest runs — above your recent median (~311ms) — indicating potential stiffness or reduced elasticity that mobility can mitigate.

recommendations.action: Insert a full rest day before your next run exceeding 8km — no walking, no cycling, no standing workouts.
recommendations.reason: You’ve done back-to-back 11km runs with only 5 days between; your VO2 max remained stable (37→38) but recovery metrics (e.g., HRV not provided) are unmonitored — proactive rest preserves adaptation.

weekly_focus.description: Balance your recent gains in intensity and efficiency with intentional low-HR volume and movement quality — reinforcing endurance capacity while protecting against accumulated fatigue.
suggested_sessions: 6km progressive run: first 3km Z2, last 3km Z3 (HR 145–150 bpm)
